'''Claude Georges Itzykson''' (11 April 1938&nbsp;– 22&nbsp;May 1995) was a French [[theoretical physicist]] who worked in [[quantum field theory]] and [[statistical mechanics]].<ref name="Brezin">{{cite journal| last1=Brezin| first1=E.| author-link1=Édouard Brézin| title=Claude Itzykson| journal=Physics Today| volume=49| issue=3| year=1996| pages=125–126| issn=0031-9228| doi=10.1063/1.2807560| bibcode=1996PhT....49c.125B| doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Zuber">{{cite web |last1=Zuber |first1=J-B |title=Claude Georges Itzykson (1938–1995) |url=http://www.annales.org/archives/x/itzykson.html |website=www.annales.org |publisher=Les Annales des Mines |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130112065418/http://www.annales.org/archives/x/itzykson.html |archive-date=12 January 2013 |date=1996 |access-date=28 October 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Biography==
Separated from his parents by [[World War II]], his father was taken to a Nazi concentration camp and Itzykson is raised in a Jewish orphanage in [[Maisons-Laffitte]].<ref name="Zuber"/> After studying at the [[Lycée Condorcet]] Itzykson graduated from the [[Ecole Polytechnique]] in 1959. He joined the Theoretical Physics Department of the [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre|CEA]] in [[Saclay]] in 1962,<ref name="Brezin"/> then headed by [[Claude Bloch]].<ref name="Zuber"/> He spent most of his career at Saclay, except for numerous visiting positions he held throughout his working life, such as at the [[Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton]].<ref name="Brezin"/><ref name="IAS">{{cite web | title=Claude Itzykson | website=Institute for Advanced Study | url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/claude-itzykson | access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>

==Works==
He was a specialist in [[quantum field theory]] and applications of [[group theory]] in physics.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Itzykson |first1=Claude |last2=Drouffe |first2=Jean-Michel |last3=Zuber |first3=Jean Bernard |title=The mathematical beauty of physics: a memorial volume for Claude Itzykson |date=1997 |publisher=World Scientific |location=Singapore |isbn=978-981-02-2807-1|lccn=97003545|oclc=36260869}}</ref> In particular, he worked on the symmetries of the [[hydrogen atom]],<ref>{{harvp|Bander|Itzykson|1966}}</ref> the discretization of network [[gauge theories]],<ref>See for example {{harvs|txt|last=Balian|last2=Drouffe|last3=Itzykson|year=1974|year2=1975}} & {{harvp|Drouffe|Itzykson|1978}}</ref> the integrals on large matrices<ref>See for example {{harvp|Brézin|Itzykson|Parisi|Zuber|1993}} and {{harvp|Itzykson|Zuber|1980b}}</ref> and their applications to problems of combinatorics<ref>{{harvp|Bessis|Itzykson|Zuber|1980}}</ref> and physics of random surfaces,<ref>{{harvp|Drouffe|Itzykson|1984}}</ref> and [[conformal field theories]] and their classification.<ref>{{harvp|Itzykson|Drouffe|1989b}}</ref>

His first works were done in collaboration with Maurice Jacob and [[Raymond Stora]].<ref name="Zuber"/> In 1980 he published a treatise on quantum field theory with [[Jean-Bernard Zuber]] that became a staple textbook on the subject.<ref name="Brezin"/><ref>{{harvp|Itzykson|Zuber|1980}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 1995 Itzykson received the [[Ampère Prize]] of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Zuber"/>
